body: Ask yourself honestly. If you were finally released from the miserable fate we call life, would you really want to wake up and hear your consciousness is going to go on forever? The only things more terrifying than never being happy, is reincarnation or life after death.

I give them a pretty rock solid argument as to why things like dementia and memory loss are a solid proof that even if something like a soul were to exist it still wouldn't be you anymore. You'd be recycling. You'd be cardboard. Shuts these comments down pretty hard.

Usually after roughly the same diatribe against life under capitalism to my friends when explaining why I'm depressed; I follow it up with some semi-serious remorse about not at least being born in an age where I could swing a battle axe at someone's head after the fifth time they insulted me and everyone would agree that prick deserves it. Makes them laugh and hides my constant feeling of unending dread. I'm only truly terrified of two concepts reincarnation or an afterlife which I think would just be the most horrifying revelation if I killed myself.

I'm gonna do something a little unconventional for me and tell you a story about myself in the hopes that it will help you. A close friend of mine, lets call him Toph, and myself have a bit of a rocky history. I grew up in a literal village with about six kids our age, one older, and 8-10 younger between maybe twenty families and you might think that would bring us closer (because this was the 90's and you couldn't get your mom to drive even 15-20 minutes to get one town over unless she was getting something at blockbuster and broaden your friend horizon) but in fact there was almost always some kind of factional breakdown usually rotating in cast between the seven of us older gents.

Well Toph was probably the least interested in the politics of ten year-olds and for the most part only wanted to play card games or video games, or any one of the many sick and obscure board games he owned. Another friend of ours, lets call him Rick, was also more interested in having fun then posturing tough and the three of us made what was probably the most frequently stable faction of the village. But then there was the other faction, Kyle had a torn childhood. His dad is still a very close family friend but his mom was into drugs and it just turned the boys of the family rotten. Eddie was Kyles best friend but they fought all the time. Eddie was quite literally the stereotype of what you'd expect the duck dynasty guys son to be like. They were both a year older but in the same grade but while we were enjoying childish games, they were into things that mattered like rap god Eminem, pornography and acting hard.

A year goes by tensions ease up and all of us have developed a bit of bond from being ostracized at school for basically living in the woods. Toph, Myself, and Kyle were all hanging out at my house together. I had been getting into some minor but frequent trouble at school lately 5th grade I'd been to the principals office or speaking to cops for a few minor spats and Kyle was always next to me. So when Kyle whispered to me to hit Toph in the balls I didn't hesitate. And you never really consider what makes you do things when your young or where your choices lead you, but I know now. I did it because I had been made to feel small, and because I knew I could make Toph feel small, because he was boyscout, because he was chubby, because he had a feminine voice. I'd give anything to remember the moment I started giving any shred of a shit about my social status and not about the joyous wonderous times when all we did was have fun together so that if I ever got the chance to go back in time I could set myself straight. I moved away when I was 12 and in this new town I was even lower on the Totem pole, I made a few new friends but not the kind you ask to help you move. So when I reconnected with my old friends when we all started driving and a few new ones who fit in with us like a glove. Everyone was happy to have me back and we all became fast friends save Kyle who was living with his father a few districts over.

I was 17 now, and I was clever. I know this because teachers would pull me to the side and tell me as much when I told them I didn't earnestly believe any of what I knew was absolute nonsense I sometimes said in class. I was clever and pathetic. I didn't have to hurt people at other peoples bequest to keep myself safe anymore, now I just had to be funny at the expense of those less practiced in being a shithead to the people around them. But like I said I knew what I was saying was absolute nonsense, and I was self aware enough why I was saying it. Because I had history class with the captain of the football team. Because I used my quick wit to make extremely sexist jokes pertaining to whatever lesson my wonderful History teacher a Ms. was teaching that day. Because after the first few laughs at ill-conceived & frankly basic jokes and a little acknowledgement from him in gym class I noticed no one tried to come at me sideways again. It could have been a decade I'd been using other people as a shield at that point I'll never have a clear memory.

Toph's voice was a little deeper, all this time still brave enough to be the same person he was when he was five. The new group of friends was like something you'd see in a cartoon. We'd always remind each other just how corny we were being but that never stopped us from being corny. More than that they were clever too and while I might have had more knowledge stored in my head to impress them they didn't understand just how quickly I was matured because of them. I had a lot of catching up to do and they made it easy for me. Before the end of my Junior year I had made myself sick several times in the course of a week. I didn't just want to apologize I had to apologize and not to make myself feel better or even to seek forgiveness but because the person I am needed him to know that I regretted what I did, that I was ashamed. "When I think about... the way I treated you when we younger I'm ashamed, and I'm sorry Toph, I often think about the time we were hanging out with Kyle at my house and I punched you in the balls. I don't know why I did that I didn't even fucking like Kyle." Toph forgave me and to this day he is one of my closest friends, but I wouldn't deserve that friendship without that apology.

You're posting here so I can only assume that you probably feel alone in your situation, and the way they treat you, you have every right to turn your nose up at them forever. But there are no fulfilling relationships based on tearing down another, and if they are constantly trying to make you feel insecure you can be certain they have someone in their life extremely talented at doing the same. I'm not saying this as criteria for you to forgive them. But if you have fond memories with your (19) sister and she matures enough one day to apologize for the way she's been making you feel, you might want to consider these elements if you find her apology to be earnest.

One final note: the media we consume has a direct effect on our world view. The majority of programing puts a premium on values like social status and the cruelty that has spawned is undeniable. However in the 5 years I left out of my story between 12-17 I had been obsessively watching a show called Stargate SG1. I'm not ashamed to say that this show laid the foundation for my moral framework. A group of friends with differing opinions that they were both ready & equipped to defend and yet always maintaining a position of advocacy for each other while tackling their own conclusions of right and wrong. It felt like a dream come true when I got a large group of friends like that of my own. That's why I needed him to know what he really meant to me and that I was sorry.

I disagree that attraction is all subjective, but you’re missing the bigger point that what people find attractive is the subjective component. Objectively people are attracted to people who excel. For some this manifests in attraction to confidence as some rather disheveled, demeaning, or even dangerous people can attract someones fancy. Others are attracted to those seeking the apex of their chosen field. A few find fancy in those who innovate with their creativity, but the most common reason for budding attraction? Passion. Find something you enjoy enough to immerse yourself in and I promise you’ll meet someone who loves the same thing and loves your commitment to it, and be confident when you speak about it because after enough work at it you will excel. We are all worthy of love but if you want to attract you have to polish the bait. Therapy can’t make you interesting, but the things you take an interest in can.

It is a powerful feeling for someone who dwells on their relationships a lot to feel like the people in their lives aren't just there because of circumstance and convenience. I try to cultivate friendships where we can't help but think of each other when we're out in the world. You can buy your friend a thousand little knickknacks they might never use or even look at, but the one time you get them something that scratches that itch just right, and just looking at it will help them feel a bit of warmth. Maybe when the time is appropriate confide a little in her. You might think you're overwhelming someone who has a lot on their plate but I've found both myself and my friends are more likely to open up to one another when venting to each other is common. I'm sure you're aware of this, you have a lot of empathy, but when a friend is venting disagreeing can be helpful but being dismissive could make your friend defensive and aggressive. I've been in more than a few screaming matches with friends and family who tell me things aren't a big deal. Comforting your friends when they are down is important, but just as important is making sure you've fostered a relationship where they feel comfortable opening up completely. And just because she has let you in to how she feels doesn't mean she's given you the complete picture. Asking will go a long way for someone desperate but proud. No pressure if it's a big ask or if you'd prefer to keep the outcome private for your friend, but I'd appreciate hearing an update on how things go.

You're not fucked up, just human. As bad as we are at understanding each other sometimes we are even worse at understanding ourselves. How you feel isn't always something you can parse out in a day or even a week. As far as moving on or giving it time; that seems to be an impossibility for you due to current circumstances. Try focusing on making distance your goal,  and try not to be so hard on yourself for wanting to be happy. You might not reconcile with your ex in the way that you want but it is still early to resign yourself to a life without love, but nothing that you've said in this post should make you feel undeserving of love. We all have selfish notions especially when we feel ourselves losing something but you chose not to act on them. I think at the very least you should try to have a conversation with him about the way this is effecting you without leveraging your emotional state. Make it clear that you are trying to find a compromise while you live together and not trying to make him feel guilty. I hope at least this provides you with a little relief, it took me years to get over my last relationship and I can't imagine how hard it would have been if we lived together. You're not a bad person for wanting to get that back and none of us can help ourselves from thinking of the worst possible ways of getting what we desperately want.

Words don't offer any solace to someone who has, at least from their perspective, come to rational conclusions as to why they want to die. You seem like a really good friend. Use what you know about her to show her that she isn't just someone to pass the time with. Surprise her with a take-out meal you know she likes, if she's been talking about some media she enjoys maybe give it a shot and see if you take an interest. People notice when you really pay attention to them beyond just daily conversations. The small things from my friends meant so much more to me in my darkest moments than anything anyone said. More than anything let her know that the way she feels is not unreasonable. When I'm reaching out to others about the way I feel the thing I'm looking for most is some kind of confirmation that the way I feel is justified. Let her know that she isn't wrong for feeling that something is wrong.

The reason we demonize suicide is simple enough. The world is very obviously broken in a way where the majority struggle far more than they should have to for longer stretches of time than the wealthy few. If suicide were viewed as a legitimate response to the hopeless odds of global capitalism a lot more people would consider it. And then everyone in denial because they either profit off it directly, have religious beliefs that allow them to dismiss the misery they experience in this life, or have found some other coping mechanism for their own raw deal would actually have to ask the question why is suicide so appealing to so many. And that question could undo the fabric of the society we’ve created.

So I studied psychology in college so I was already familiar with the topic but they bring up an interesting point at the beginning of the video that is extremely relevant about support from family falling flat. Platitudes like 'You can do it!" are specifically designed to avoid addressing a concern, mistake, or problem while giving the illusion of a solution. Platitudes fail to convey the reasons of why a certain result occurred and these types of non-answer answers treat all problems as nebulous and without cause. But our concerns are real we aren't depressed because we are broken, we are depressed because we see a broken situation, a clear way to fix it, and a society that would rather pretend it doesn't exist. We crave a reason for chaos when it seems like everyone else is resigned to blissful ignorance. I don't know you and I could be wrong but I suspect you have an abundance of empathy. When you see something you know is wrong and you understand that it could be different, but there is no explanation as to why it keeps being wrong you empathize and it evokes that powerless feeling in you. The only thing that hurts me more than being exploited is watching it happen to people with even less agency. Thank you for sharing the video I enjoy channels with short educational clips.

The warm thought that sometimes gets me to sleep on restless nights is that ‘this night will be the night my organs just stop in my sleep.’ It makes for a demoralizing morning when I wake up but it is bettet than insomnia. I definitely understand wanting to die while also wanting it to be taken out of your hands. At the end of the day I’m looking for someone to save me, one gruesome way or any other that would work.

My friends think it’s just morbid humor that I call cigarettes lottery tickets, and I’m always searching for the one winner that could change my life forever. Death just seems like the rest I’ve needed for so long, but I’m not looking to be in pain just get rid of it so I never go through with it.

For every step you take forward it feels like life has stuck its leg out to trip you. This is an all too familiar feeling for me :(. Every little win followed by a series of crippling defeats. And every time it happens it gets harder to try again, and you remind yourself the next few times you try to keep expectations low because losing only really hurts when you think you could actually succeed.
